Formaldehyde (PFA) alone often produces a characteristic class of “phantom” or “HOT” peaks in transcription-factor ChIP-seq experiments.  
•  PFA readily cross-links DNA that is already nucleosome-depleted and occupied by large multi-protein assemblies such as the transcription machinery.  
•  As a result, highly accessible chromatin—especially active promoters and enhancers—can be pulled down even with antibodies that are not truly bound there, giving rise to artifactual peaks that look the same for many different TFs.  

Including DSG, a protein–protein cross-linker, strengthens genuine TF–chromatin contacts while not improving (and often diminishing) the non-specific capture of open chromatin. Therefore those PFA-only “phantom” peaks typically vanish when DSG is added.

Hence, the peaks that disappear on switching from PFA to PFA+DSG are most often the spurious enrichments at actively transcribed regulatory regions.

Answer: D
